issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify getTotalNumberOfStudents() as a parameterless method returning the total number of students. The solution implementation defines getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) — i.e. it requires a boolean parameter. This parameter mismatch contradicts the specification and will confuse students (and tests) about the expected method signature and usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem specification by providing a parameterless getTotalNumberOfStudents() method that returns the sum of inscribed and guest students. If a variant that optionally excludes guests is desired, implement it as a separate helper (e.g., getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) private) or overload with an internal call, but ensure the public API matches the UML and problem statement.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a no-argument method getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests). This changes the public API and expected usage of the method: students following the exercise will implement or look for a no-arg method returning the total number of students, while the provided solution requires a boolean parameter to include guest students. The signature mismatch creates confusion mapping the requirement to the reference implementation and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the API across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to implement the no-argument method getTotalNumberOfStudents() that returns the total number of students (including guests) to match the UML/problem, or (B) update the problem statement and UML to declare getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests): int (and document the parameter) so the boolean parameter in the solution is explicit. Alternatively, provide an overloaded no-arg getTotalNumberOfStudents() that delegates to getTotalNumberOfStudents(true) to preserve both behaviors.
